findings.summary: The accepted reading has no intended-refusal criterion, so the replay will hold the job and the verdict fails. The plan's step 1 therefore stops the producer straight away.
findings.evidence: I read run/mod.rs. The replay runs on every job whose checks pass (replay_run, 2814-2847), using ctx.reading.acceptance_criteria, and the comment at 2468 says 'A held replay fails the verdict (`judge`)'. replay_is_held (reading.rs:2647) is `newly*100 > total*10 && !intended`. `intended` is criteria_intend_higher_refusal, which matches only the INTENDED_REFUSAL_PHRASES (2619-2628: 'refuse more', 'higher refusal rate', 'more readings are refused', ...). None of the reading's six criteria uses any of those phrases. No stored reading has a 'Code survey:' assumption, so every stored change reading of class code or tests with a behavior criterion is newly refused. That share is very likely above 10% of the 50-reading window (an estimate: I could not count, because records/ is absent). The planner saw this correctly. But step 1 checks a condition that is already false, so the producer would stop before making any edit. Fix: Athena or the user should amend the reading's criteria before planning again. Add one criterion that uses a listed phrase, for example: 'The change refuses more readings: change readings of class code or tests with a behavior criterion and no Code survey assumption are refused; a higher refusal rate is intended.' Then re-plan, keeping step 1 as a guard.
findings.location: Reading acceptance criteria 1-6; plan Decision 6, Step 1, Open question 1; crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs:2465-2469, 2814-2847; crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs:2619-2649, 2694-2738

findings.summary: Signal C ('any criterion text containing records/') fires on criteria that only mention records/ to exclude it, such as 'records/ is not changed'.
findings.evidence: Matching a bare substring in criterion text is a crude heuristic. A criterion stating that records/ stays untouched would demand allow-list evidence for no reason. Fix: Drop signal C. Or limit it to deliverables and to criteria that also name a new record kind or a records.rs change. Signals A and B already cover a new stored record kind.

findings.summary: Matching a single keyword ('allow-list', 'round trip') lets a survey pass by mentioning the term in passing, even in a negation.
findings.evidence: The plan admits this under Risks. Criterion 3 literally asks for naming, so a keyword check meets the letter of it. A survey saying 'no allow-list change' would still pass. Fix: Require `check_record_file` or `AnyRecord`, or a named test function or path for the round-trip test. Keep the content judgement with the verifier, as the plan already says.

findings.summary: `git diff --stat` may not be available wherever the verifier runs it.
findings.evidence: System facts say readers, planners and critics get plain copies without git. The verifier's environment is not stated. Fix: Phrase the check as 'the change's file list contains only reading.rs, briefs.rs and CHANGELOG.md', and leave the tool to the verifier.

request_reading_mismatch: The reading misses a direct consequence of the fix it asks for. A new refusal rule in check_reading_acceptance newly refuses stored change/code readings during the replay, and the reading's criteria never say that a higher refusal rate is intended. The replay therefore holds the job (run/mod.rs:2468; reading.rs:2647), and the request's acceptance condition ('fmt, clippy and test pass' plus a passing verdict) cannot be met. The reading needs one criterion that uses an INTENDED_REFUSAL_PHRASES phrase.
summary: The plan is otherwise sound and grounded in code I read. check_reading_acceptance (reading.rs:2229) is the right place for the rule. check_criteria_evidence, check_reading_text, INTENDED_REFUSAL_PHRASES, the scoped_reading helper (4278), READING_RULES ([&str; 4] at briefs.rs:1460), reader_brief, reader_inputs and the rule-line test all exist where the plan says. The demonstrations call the real check through its entry point and would fail without the change. However, the replay runs on every job (run/mod.rs replay_run), and a held replay fails the verdict. The new rule refuses every stored change reading of class code or tests that has a behavior criterion. The accepted reading has no intended-refusal criterion, so the job will be held, and the plan's own step 1 stops the producer before any edit. The planner cannot fix this, because it is a gap in the reading's criteria. I reject until Athena or the user adds an intended-refusal criterion. Minor soundness points: signal C fires on any mention of records/, and a single keyword is enough to satisfy the evidence rule.
